title: Sleeping in a Coffin
hook: What if you slept in a coffin?

beats.label: After a few hours
beats.line: CO2 rises, and your head throbs with pressure.
beats.idea: Cartoon shows character inside coffin, breath clouds turning green, head with pressure lines

beats.label: By the end of day one
beats.line: Oxygen falls, and your heart races to pull in more air.
beats.idea: Close‑up of heart beating faster, oxygen meter low

beats.label: After two days
beats.line: Your calves seize up, delivering sharp, painful cramps.
beats.idea: Legs show tight muscles and little sparkles indicating cramps

beats.label: By a week
beats.line: A sore forms on your scalp, and you toss restlessly.
beats.idea: Zoom on skin with red dots, character tossing restlessly

beats.label: After a month
beats.line: Your blood volume drops, and standing makes you dizzy.
beats.idea: Skeleton inside shows slightly thinner bones, character wobbling as he exits

description: A quick look at how a night in a coffin affects your body.

facts.claim: Carbon dioxide buildup in a sealed space can cause head pressure and lightheadedness
Low oxygen levels cause the heart to beat faster to deliver oxygen
Prolonged immobility leads to muscle stiffness and cramps
Extended pressure on skin can cause pressure spots (pressure ulcers)
Lack of movement for a month can cause a small loss in bone density
facts.source: Mayo Clinic, Bone loss due to immobilization

end.line: Would you still choose the coffin?

topic: What happens if you sleep in a coffin?
